goals.h1: Menopause treatments, compared with what clinics sell.
goals.description: Estradiol, estradiol with progesterone and fezolinetant (Veozah) are FDA approved for menopause hot flashes. Compounded hormones are not. What each one is.
goals.short_answer: No peptide is FDA approved for menopause symptoms, and none on our lists is sold for them. The FDA-approved options are estradiol, alone or with progesterone, and one non-hormonal pill, fezolinetant (Veozah). Compounded hormones are made by pharmacies and are not FDA approved, so the FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.
goals.legal_note: Approved means the FDA approved a product containing it for a stated use. Compounded means a pharmacy made it; a compounded drug is not FDA approved, even when an approved product has the same ingredient.
